what_it_does: When designing an AI accelerator chip, engineers must choose both the neural network architecture (the layers, sizes, and connectivity) and the hardware design together to get the best performance—a problem called co-search. Current methods are slow because they actually train candidate networks to see if they work, which takes hours or days. UniCoS solves this by introducing a training-free accuracy predictor that estimates how well a network will perform in seconds, without any training. It also uses clustering to efficiently explore the space of possible hardware designs. Together, these innovations enable rapid joint exploration of both CNN (traditional image networks) and Vision Transformers (newer networks based on attention mechanisms) alongside hardware accelerator designs.
